topic: Template Function Operator Overloading for std::array Inequality
explanation: This concept demonstrates how to overload operators for template classes in C++, specifically the inequality operator (!=) for the standard container std::array. By defining a template function, we enable comparison operations between arrays of any element type T and size N, leveraging C++'s template system to write generic, type-safe code that works across different instantiations of std::array. This approach exemplifies modern C++'s emphasis on generic programming, enabling flexible and reusable code components.
syntax:
template <class T, size_t N>
bool operator!=(const std::array<T, N>& x, const std::array<T, N>& y);
example_explanation: This example defines a template function that overloads the '!=' operator for std::array objects of any element type T and size N. In main(), two arrays are created and compared using this operator. Since the arrays differ in the last element, the function returns true, and the program outputs 'Arrays are not equal.' This demonstrates how operator overloading with templates allows for generic, type-safe comparison operations across different array types, exemplifying modern C++'s emphasis on generic programming and operator customization.
